objective: Exploratory exact enumeration. For a frozen family of uniform rules (circulant rules on pairs and on triples, symmetric rules, and small lattice controls), compute each rule's shape under the strict and the competition readings, its bonds and ties, and the separation of every pair (the size of the smallest bond or tie containing it). Report which shapes have near and far, and whether separation follows the rule's own layout. Pairwise rules can have a bond only under competition, so any pairwise rule with near and far under competition is a signal for a confirmatory follow-up.
status: Closed: supported by KNOT-COMPETITION-20261019-001B-E002 (confirmatory) after the exploratory census E001. Strict reading: rules on pairs never give a bond, so no near and far. Competition: 178 of 470 circulant pairwise rules give near and far, never more than two levels, following the layout, flattening it on frustrated rings, or singling out antipodes. On triangle strips and rings counted per triangle, competition equals strict not-all-equal knots on the triangles and separation grows with layout distance (3 to 8 at 14 vertices); counted per pair, it collapses to few ordered states with at most two levels. Near and far is always inherited from a layout.
title: Near and far under both readings: a census of uniform rules
